summary: Built the one maths core in lines (0.8.5). workbench/math_ranges.py (pure, Fraction only): Enclosure, outward, enclose, decide, check_box, corner_witness, allowed, freed. workbench/math_answers.py: the record ledger.math-answer/1 (inputs with origin, source and tolerance, result, state, for_all, witness, guarantee, at most 8 derivation steps, freshness, words, own implementation hashes, model_calls 0, digest), ask()/answer() that never raise, bindings_from_problem over math_service.model_for, and the Kernel op math.answer (read). workbench/tolerances.py: ledger.tolerance/1 with tolerances.get/list (read) and tolerances.set (approve), states APPLIES / CARRIED_OVER / RECHECK computed on read. stac_bridge: math_ir for solve, range and check (strict shell words, at most 40, steps in order, at most four given), calculate unchanged to math.preview, freshness attached to every MATH result. Registered in engineering_kernel and engineering_cli like schedule_math. ALWAYS_ASKS row for tolerances.set with the design's words. A provider (model) plan that carries a given range is refused in stacy_control.validate_actions. On screen: a maths line typed to Kasandra or the Terminal answers in words (Holds / Does not hold / Cannot tell for checks; Solve for NAME; Range; Worked out), numbers to four figures with the exact value beside, and a "see the receipt" word that shows the inputs with their revisions, the method, the guarantee and the freshness. docs/INTEGRATED_I02.md has the grammar and three worked examples on Rail Demo numbers, run word for word by a test. Frozen maths files untouched. All 26 in-scope vectors are tests; the tier-1 list (73 modules) passed in both looks.

decisions: A step lattice has offset 0 (the multiples of S in the declared unit); an integer quantity gets step 1. The design names an offset o but not where it comes from.

The solve guard reads "never under a division or a power" literally: a ranged quantity anywhere under a division (either side) or a power gives UNSUPPORTED with its reason. Conservative and sound; a numerator-only case could be allowed later.
solve with != is UNSUPPORTED ("Not equal leaves two pieces; ask with < or > instead"); solve takes one relation (the design's "up to 8 relations" is not built).

Rounding: a range is rounded outward (low end down, high end up); an allowed end of a solve is rounded toward the inside (down for an upper end) so a shown number never claims more than is allowed. The exact value is always beside it; an exact decimal of six figures or fewer is shown as it is.

state is HOLDS / FAILS / UNDECIDED for a relation; ANSWERED for a stage that asks no yes-or-no question (calculate or range of a quantity, solve, whose ALLOWED / WHOLE_DOMAIN / EMPTY is in result.allowed.state); otherwise the error state.

The owner's tolerances apply automatically to range, check and solve when APPLIES or CARRIED_OVER; a given in the line wins for that quantity; calculate stays at the declared values. A RECHECK tolerance is shown in the receipt and not applied.

One tolerance record per (problem, variable); saying it again makes a new revision. tolerances.set is bound to the sheet's revision and context digest like other problem actions, and needs a non-blank basis.
The planner rule ("never produces given") is enforced where every model plan is checked: stacy_control.validate_actions refuses a provider plan whose stac.* program or math.answer carries a given.
The witness is the corner furthest from holding, re-evaluated by math_model.evaluate; the words name only the ranged quantities of that corner.

Rail Demo build() is unchanged (no problem sheet added, REVISION unchanged): the docs examples run on a problem sheet the test makes from rail_demo.READINGS and LIMITS_B (12 V, 250 mA, the Rev B 4 W limit).
The calculate line still compiles to math.preview exactly as before; stac_bridge adds freshness to its result. math.answer also accepts stage calculate when called directly.
The Terminal shows a maths answer unwrapped like any other result (with wrap_output the answer showed as a highlighted block).

release_note: Maths in lines: a line on a problem sheet can now solve for a quantity ("up to 500 mA, at 12 V and the limit"), give the exact range of an expression over ranges, and check a limit, answering Holds, Does not hold or Cannot tell in plain words, with each number to four figures and its exact value beside it. Every answer has its receipt one word away: the inputs with their revisions, how it was worked out, what is guaranteed, and whether the sheet's sources changed since, so a stale limit is never used silently. Tolerances are yours: you set them and they wait for your Approve, Kasandra never makes up a range, and a tolerance whose value has since changed waits for your recheck instead of being applied. Everything is worked in exact fractions; SymPy and Z3 are not needed.
